Thesis.proseOnly: Opening case carries the decision (the 8.71 s step decomposition); the figures live in the sections that derive each term.

The Scale Moment.teaches: Fleet counts climb ~4 orders while compute climbs ~7 — the gap between the two ladders is per-device rate, and ~half the compute growth is count×duration.
The Scale Moment.source: Compute trend decomposition + cluster-size landmarks (2 GTX 580 → 10k V100 → 16,384 H100).

From Single Node to Fleet.teaches: The 8.71 s step split into compute / bubble / exchange: the two non-compute terms are what fleet growth taxes first, and why doubling N cannot halve wall-clock.

AI Scaling Laws.proseOnly: The power-law relationship and its breakdown regimes are carried by the scaling-law equation and the compute-orders chart.

Constraints of Scale.teaches: Per-device MTTF divides by N under independent failures: 50,000 h on one GPU becomes ~2 h at 25,000 GPUs, matching Llama 3's measured ~1 interruption per 3.1 h.
Constraints of Scale.source: MTBF arithmetic + the Llama 3 405B production interruption record.

The C³ Taxonomy.teaches: D·A·M names the workload; C³ names what the fleet spends the step doing. Map each optimization to the term it relieves — a faster chip only relieves Compute.
The C³ Taxonomy.source: The C³ projection: Compute, Communication, Coordination as the fleet's verbs.

The Fleet Stack and Lighthouse Archetype.proseOnly: The four bands and three archetypes are organizing prose; the archetypes get full treatment in their own chapters.

Fallacies and Pitfalls.proseOnly: Each fallacy reuses a worked number from earlier sections — no new mechanism to draw.
